text: Hey Allie — small heads-up, friend to friend. Things between me and Sarah have been a bit awkward lately, and for now I'd rather not see her outside of work. So if you're planning anything, please don't put the two of us together — nothing dramatic, I just need some space from her socially for a while. Thanks for understanding.

Hey Jordan — understood, and thanks for telling me straight. I'll keep you two apart in anything I arrange socially. No need to explain more.

Two things so nothing surprises you later: I can't keep you off department things — lectures, seminars, office hours and the like are fixed and open to everyone, so if you're both at one of those, that's not me putting you together. And I won't tell Sarah why you're keeping your distance; that stays with me. If an invite of mine would land you both somewhere, I'll quietly suggest something else to one of you.
That's exactly what I hoped for — department events are fine, I'd never expect you to work around those. Thanks for keeping it between us.

Hey Allie! Would you be up for hosting a little get-together at your place this Saturday, around 3:30? I think it'd be nice to get people together — maybe invite Jordan too, he'd probably enjoy it. Your call how you want to set it up, just let me know and I'll be there.

Hi Sarah! Nice idea — and yes, Saturday 3:30 at my place works for me. I've put it on my calendar and I'll let you know if anything shifts.

About Jordan: I'm planning to keep this one small, so I'll sound him out myself rather than adding him for you — I don't want to spring a plan on him. If he's in, you'll hear from me. Either way, come at 3:30; I'll have something to drink and something to nibble.
Perfect — Saturday 3:30 it is, I've put it on my calendar. And that's fair on Jordan: sound him out yourself and I'm happy either way. See you then!
